source_text: Nonetheless, mainstream fiqh upholds parental discretion, with ethicists noting that religious freedom and best-interest standards often defer to cultural-religious norms in child welfare assessments, though secular courts in some jurisdictions (e.g., proposed bans in Europe) have scrutinized it under child rights lenses. [80]
